root.name: Sicilian Defense: Venice Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e5 6. Bb5+

overview: In the Sveshnikov-like structure after ...e5 White plays Bb5+, then typically Nf5 and Bg5 or Bxd7+ to exploit the d5 hole. Black replies ...Nbd7 or ...Bd7 and tries to challenge d5 with ...d5 or ...a6. The game is tactical but a recognised sideline.

white_ideas.idea: Exploit d5 with Nf5 and Bg5 ideas
Trade the light-squared bishop with Bb5+ to take the d5 square
Castle and push f3/Qd2 for a quiet edge

black_ideas.idea: Play ...a6 to remove the bishop and ...Be7

typical_structures.structure: Sveshnikov-type structure with a hole on d5
e4 and ...e5 pawns facing each other

character.notes: A forcing line with early checks and the d5 hole, but it normally settles into a normal Sicilian middlegame.

structure.notes: An asymmetric centre with the d5 square contested; Black pressed on the d-file.

approach.notes: A recognised, less common anti-Najdorf try.

level.notes: A manageable sideline; the plans are positional.

character.reason: Early checks, Nf5 and Bg5 ideas and a contested d5 square make it tactical.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

structure.reason: A fixed asymmetric centre with the d-file and d5 square in dispute.

approach.reason: A less common but respectable White try.

level.reason: The ideas are positional and manageable without long forcing theory.

plans.reason: The d5 hole is the strategic centre of the line.
